notable_absence.finding: node-init.md is the page that actually performs the step the already-promoted server:node-provisioning concept describes itself as being 'distinct from and subsequent to' - yet node-init.md never uses the word 'provisioning' or otherwise signposts that a further, separate step (setting administrator credentials, services, memory quotas, via cluster-init or server-add) still lies ahead before this node is a real cluster member. The two-step bootstrap sequence is legible from the provisioning-side concept's own description, but not from this, the earlier step's, own page - a reader arriving at node-init.md cold would not learn the step has a name or a defined successor.

cross_component_finding: This exact batch documents the cluster/node IP-family setting through three different flag shapes across three sibling pages: node-init.md exposes it as four independent boolean switches (--ipv4, --ipv6, --ipv4only, --ipv6only, no hyphen before 'only'); cluster-init.md exposes it as a single valued flag (--ip-family <ipv4|ipv6|ipv4-only|ipv6-only>, WITH a hyphen before 'only' in the enum values); and ip-family.md (this same batch) exposes it as --get/--set plus --ipv4/--ipv4only/--ipv6/--ipv6only (matching node-init's no-hyphen shape, not cluster-init's hyphenated enum). All three configure the same already-promoted server:cluster-address-family concept, but no page cross-references the other two flag shapes or explains why the value spelling differs between 'ipv4-only' and 'ipv4only' depending on which subcommand you're using - a concrete, checkable terminology/shape-drift instance across near-identical siblings, exactly this round's framing hypothesis.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none - node-init is a self-managed Server bootstrap step (disk paths, hostname, IP family for node-to-node communication) with no Capella analog stated or implied on this page.
